items.title: Measure-theoretic mutual information
items.statement: For a joint probability law P on E×F with marginals P_E and P_F, define I(E;F)=D(P||P_E⊗P_F) in nats, allowing +∞.
items.strategy: Define the law functional directly through directional measurable-space KL and the product of the two marginals; keep the value extended nonnegative and do not express it as a difference of entropies.
items.axiom_base: AC is inherited from the published measurable-space KL definition through its Radon–Nikodym density.

references.title: Robert M. Gray, Entropy and Information Theory, corrected author-hosted first edition, Chapter 5 §§5.2–5.5
Yury Polyanskiy and Yihong Wu, MIT 6.441 Information Theory, Chapter 2 §§2.1–2.4
John Duchi, Lecture Notes on Statistics and Information Theory, Chapter 2 §2.1

items.title: Finite-alphabet KL agrees with measurable-space KL
items.statement: On a finite measurable alphabet, the published probability-vector KL and the measurable-space KL coincide, including the support-mismatch +∞ convention.
items.strategy: Check the Radon–Nikodym derivative atom by atom when absolute continuity holds; treat a positive-mass atom with zero reference mass separately.
items.axiom_base: AC is required only by the general KL definition and its Radon–Nikodym supplier; the finite sum and atomwise density check are finite.

references.title: Robert M. Gray, Entropy and Information Theory, corrected author-hosted first edition, Chapter 5 §§5.2 and 5.5
John Duchi, Lecture Notes on Statistics and Information Theory, Chapter 2 §2.1

items.title: KL is invariant under a measurable bijection
items.statement: For a measurable bijection with measurable inverse, push-forward preserves the directional measurable-space KL divergence, including the singular +∞ case.
items.strategy: Transport a Radon–Nikodym density through the inverse bijection; a measurable null set witnessing singularity transports in the non-absolutely-continuous case.
items.axiom_base: AC is inherited from the Radon–Nikodym definition of general KL.

references.title: Robert M. Gray, Entropy and Information Theory, corrected author-hosted first edition, Chapter 5 §5.2
Yury Polyanskiy and Yihong Wu, MIT 6.441 Information Theory, Chapter 3 §3.1

items.title: Conditional KL for supplied probability kernels
items.statement: For a common probability base μ and probability kernels K,L into one standard Borel target, define D_μ(K||L)=∫D(K_z||L_z)μ(dz), with singular fibers contributing +∞.
items.strategy: Use a supplied pair of kernels and common base measure; justify measurability of the fiber divergence by the local variational representation theorem.
items.axiom_base: AC is inherited through general KL and the standard-Borel countable determining-algebra supplier.

references.title: Robert M. Gray, Entropy and Information Theory, corrected author-hosted first edition, Chapter 5 §5.3
Yury Polyanskiy and Yihong Wu, MIT 6.441 Information Theory, Chapter 2 §§2.2 and 2.6

items.title: Finite-alphabet conditional entropy given an observation
items.statement: For a finite-valued X and a standard-Borel observation Y, define H(X|Y) as the P_Y average of the finite Shannon entropy of a regular conditional law of X given Y.
items.strategy: Average the bounded finite-alphabet entropy of a supplied regular conditional law; use standard-Borel disintegration and almost-everywhere uniqueness to justify the version convention.
items.axiom_base: AC is required for standard-Borel regular conditional distributions and their simultaneous almost-everywhere uniqueness.

references.title: Robert M. Gray, Entropy and Information Theory, corrected author-hosted first edition, Chapter 2 §2.5 and Chapter 5 §5.5
John Duchi, Lecture Notes on Statistics and Information Theory, Chapter 2 §2.1

items.title: The product of two probability kernels is a probability kernel
items.statement: For probability kernels K_z and L_z into standard-Borel spaces E and F, z↦K_z⊗L_z is a probability kernel into E×F.
items.strategy: The product measure exists fiberwise; a pi-lambda argument extends measurable evaluation from rectangles to the full product sigma-algebra.
items.axiom_base: The finite product-measure supplier is choice-free; no choice of versions or measures is made because each product measure is unique.

references.title: Yury Polyanskiy and Yihong Wu, MIT 6.441 Information Theory, Chapter 2 §§2.2 and 2.6
Robert M. Gray, Entropy and Information Theory, corrected author-hosted first edition, Chapter 5 §5.3

items.title: Law entropy as self-mutual information
items.statement: For a random element X, define its measure-theoretic law entropy by H(X)=I(X;X), distinct from differential entropy.
items.strategy: Use the general joint-KL definition on the diagonal joint law of (X,X); do not use differential-entropy subtraction.
items.axiom_base: AC is inherited through measurable-space KL.

references.title: Robert M. Gray, Entropy and Information Theory, corrected author-hosted first edition, Chapter 5 §5.5
John Duchi, Lecture Notes on Statistics and Information Theory, Chapter 2 §2.1

items.title: Finite-alphabet conditional entropy is version-invariant and obeys its chain rule
items.statement: For finite-valued X,U and standard-Borel Z, conditional entropy is version-independent and H(X,U|Z)=H(X|Z)+H(U|X,Z), with all terms finite.
items.strategy: Use simultaneous almost-everywhere uniqueness for version invariance, then prove the finite chain identity pointwise for each conditioning value and integrate.
items.axiom_base: AC is inherited from the regular-conditional-law existence and uniqueness interfaces.

references.title: Robert M. Gray, Entropy and Information Theory, corrected author-hosted first edition, Chapter 2 §2.5 and Chapter 5 §5.5
John Duchi, Lecture Notes on Statistics and Information Theory, Chapter 2 §2.1

items.title: Variational and finite-partition formulas for measurable-space KL
items.statement: For probability measures P,Q on one measurable space, D(P||Q) is both the supremum of E_P f−log E_Q e^f over bounded measurable f and the supremum of finite-partition KL sums.
items.strategy: Use exponentially tilted measures for the upper bound, clipped log densities or a singular-set witness for the lower bound, then optimize finite-valued functions and uniformly approximate bounded functions by simple functions.
items.axiom_base: AC is used through the Radon–Nikodym definition and the published KL equality theorem.

references.title: Robert M. Gray, Entropy and Information Theory, corrected author-hosted first edition, Chapter 5 §5.2, Theorem 5.2.1
Yury Polyanskiy and Yihong Wu, MIT 6.441 Information Theory, Chapter 3 §3.4, Theorem 3.7
John Duchi, Lecture Notes on Statistics and Information Theory, Chapter 5 §5.1, Theorem 5.1.1

items.title: Conditional KL is measurable for supplied kernels
items.statement: For probability kernels K,L into a standard-Borel target, z↦D(K_z||L_z) is measurable.
items.strategy: Reduce the variational supremum to a countable family of simple functions on a countable generating algebra; each candidate integral is measurable by the kernel integration theorem.
items.axiom_base: AC is used by the standard-Borel countable determining-algebra supplier and by measurable-space KL.

references.title: Yury Polyanskiy and Yihong Wu, MIT 6.441 Information Theory, Chapter 2 §2.6
Robert M. Gray, Entropy and Information Theory, corrected author-hosted first edition, Chapter 5 §5.3

items.title: The same-marginal conditional-product law is well-defined
items.statement: For standard-Borel X,Y,Z and supplied regular conditional laws K=P_{X|Z}, L=P_{Y|Z}, the product kernel K_z⊗L_z integrates against P_Z to a unique probability law, independent of the chosen versions.
items.strategy: Construct the product kernel and its joint law, then use simultaneous almost-everywhere uniqueness of the supplied conditional kernels and uniqueness of the joint measure.
items.axiom_base: AC is used for standard-Borel conditional-law existence and simultaneous uniqueness; finite product-kernel construction adds no choice.

references.title: Robert M. Gray, Entropy and Information Theory, corrected author-hosted first edition, Chapter 5 §§5.3 and 5.5
Yury Polyanskiy and Yihong Wu, MIT 6.441 Information Theory, Chapter 2 §§2.4 and 2.6

items.title: Self-mutual-information entropy on countable and non-atomic laws
items.statement: For a standard-Borel law supported on countably many atoms of masses p_i, H(X)=Σ_i p_i log(1/p_i), possibly +∞; if the law has positive non-atomic mass, H(X)=+∞.
items.strategy: Compute the Radon–Nikodym density on countable diagonal atoms; for non-atomic mass, exhibit a diagonal set of positive joint mass and zero product mass.
items.axiom_base: AC is inherited from self-mutual-information through measurable-space KL; countability and atom calculations are otherwise explicit.

references.title: Robert M. Gray, Entropy and Information Theory, corrected author-hosted first edition, Chapters 1 and 5 §5.5
John Duchi, Lecture Notes on Statistics and Information Theory, Chapter 2 §2.1

items.title: Conditional mutual information by a same-marginal product law
items.statement: For standard-Borel X,Y,Z, define I(X;Y|Z)=D(P_{XYZ}||P_Z⋉(P_{X|Z}⊗P_{Y|Z})), where the reference law has the same Z marginal and conditionally independent X,Y.
items.strategy: Use the uniquely defined joint law formed from the product of regular conditional marginals; its version independence makes the divergence a function of the joint law.
items.axiom_base: AC is required for standard-Borel regular conditional distributions, simultaneous versions, and measurable-space KL.

references.title: Yury Polyanskiy and Yihong Wu, MIT 6.441 Information Theory, Chapter 2 §2.4
Robert M. Gray, Entropy and Information Theory, corrected author-hosted first edition, Chapter 5 §5.5

items.title: KL chain rule for standard-Borel disintegrations
items.statement: For joint laws P(dx,dy)=μ(dx)K_x(dy) and Q(dx,dy)=ν(dx)L_x(dy) with standard-Borel factors, D(P||Q)=D(μ||ν)+∫D(K_x||L_x)μ(dx), as an equality in [0,+∞].
items.strategy: Separate singular marginal and joint cases; in the absolutely continuous case factor the joint density into the marginal density and a jointly measurable conditional density, then integrate the logarithm with finite negative parts.
items.axiom_base: AC supplies marginal and joint Radon–Nikodym densities and the countable determining algebra. Conditional kernels are supplied, not selected in the proof.

references.title: Robert M. Gray, Entropy and Information Theory, corrected author-hosted first edition, Chapter 5 §5.3, Lemmas 5.3.1–5.3.2 and Theorem 5.3.2
Yury Polyanskiy and Yihong Wu, MIT 6.441 Information Theory, Chapter 2 §2.2

items.title: Zero information is exactly independence
items.statement: For standard-Borel variables, I(X;Y)=0 iff X,Y are independent, and I(X;Y|Z)=0 iff X,Y are conditionally independent given σ(Z).
items.strategy: Apply the zero-equality criterion for KL; identify equality with the product law by checking generating rectangles and the conditional-independence factorization.
items.axiom_base: AC is inherited from KL, conditional-law existence and the conditional-independence class convention.

references.title: Robert M. Gray, Entropy and Information Theory, corrected author-hosted first edition, Chapter 2 §2.5 and Chapter 5 §5.5
Yury Polyanskiy and Yihong Wu, MIT 6.441 Information Theory, Chapter 2 §2.4, Theorem 2.5

items.title: Mutual information is approximated by finite coordinate quantizations
items.statement: Increasing finite quantizers that generate the standard-Borel coordinate sigma-algebras recover I(X;Y) and I(X;Y|Z); the conditioning variable Z is kept unchanged.
items.strategy: Apply the variational KL formula on an increasing sequence of generated sigma-algebras and show that bounded measurable functions are approximable in the finite measure P+Q.
items.axiom_base: AC is used only for the countable generating-algebra and standard-Borel conditional-law suppliers.

references.title: Robert M. Gray, Entropy and Information Theory, corrected author-hosted first edition, Chapter 5 §5.5, Lemmas 5.5.5 and 5.5.7
Yury Polyanskiy and Yihong Wu, MIT 6.441 Information Theory, Chapter 3 §3.4

items.title: Law entropy and differential entropy are different quantities
items.statement: Law entropy is self-mutual information; differential entropy is −∫f log f for a specified Euclidean density when the integral is defined, and may be finite or negative while law entropy is infinite.
items.strategy: State the two definitions and their distinct domains; use the uniform distribution example as the concrete contrast.

references.title: John Duchi, Lecture Notes on Statistics and Information Theory, Chapter 2 §2.1
Robert M. Gray, Entropy and Information Theory, corrected author-hosted first edition, Chapter 1 and Chapter 5 §5.5

items.title: Mutual information chain rule without subtracting infinities
items.statement: For standard-Borel X,Y,Z, I(X;(Y,Z))=I(X;Z)+I(X;Y|Z), with the right side an extended sum of nonnegative quantities.
items.strategy: Disintegrate against Z, apply the KL chain rule within each fiber, and integrate nonnegative KL terms; never rearrange an ∞−∞ expression.
items.axiom_base: AC is inherited from measurable-space KL and standard-Borel disintegration.

references.title: Robert M. Gray, Entropy and Information Theory, corrected author-hosted first edition, Chapter 5 §§5.3 and 5.5
John Duchi, Lecture Notes on Statistics and Information Theory, Chapter 2 §2.1

items.title: A uniform law has infinite self-information entropy and zero differential entropy
items.statement: For X uniform on [0,1], H(X)=+∞ while its differential entropy is 0.
items.strategy: Apply the non-countable-support clause and evaluate the density integral directly.

references.title: John Duchi, Lecture Notes on Statistics and Information Theory, Chapter 2 §2.1
Robert M. Gray, Entropy and Information Theory, corrected author-hosted first edition, Chapter 1 and Chapter 5 §5.5

items.title: A finite deterministic copy has mutual information equal to entropy
items.statement: If X is Bernoulli(p) and Y=X, then I(X;Y)=H(X), including p=0 and p=1.
items.strategy: Compute the joint and product masses on their two diagonal atoms and check the deterministic conditional law.

references.title: Robert M. Gray, Entropy and Information Theory, corrected author-hosted first edition, Chapter 2 §2.5
Yury Polyanskiy and Yihong Wu, MIT 6.441 Information Theory, Chapter 2 §§2.3–2.4

items.title: Coarsening the conditioning variable can increase conditional mutual information
items.statement: For X=Y fair Bernoulli and Z=(X,Y), I(X;Y|Z)=0, while conditioning on the constant coarsening of Z gives ln 2.
items.strategy: Compute the point-mass conditional product law when Z=(X,Y), then compute the ordinary fair-bit mutual information after replacing Z by a constant.

references.title: Robert M. Gray, Entropy and Information Theory, corrected author-hosted first edition, Chapter 2 §2.5
Yury Polyanskiy and Yihong Wu, MIT 6.441 Information Theory, Chapter 2 §2.4

items.title: Changing a conditional kernel on a null value does not change information
items.statement: Changing a regular conditional law at one null conditioning value can change the pointwise conditional KL there from 0 to +∞ without changing the integrated conditional mutual information.
items.strategy: Verify that the modified kernel is still a regular conditional law and that the integrated reference measure is unchanged on the null fiber.

references.title: Robert M. Gray, Entropy and Information Theory, corrected author-hosted first edition, Chapter 5 §5.3
Yury Polyanskiy and Yihong Wu, MIT 6.441 Information Theory, Chapter 2 §§2.2 and 2.6
